Also awarded in each category

Certificates of Excellence

Judges award these certificates in both the Bachelor's and the Master's category, on top of the placed prizes. One project can win more than one.

  • Excellence in Artificial IntelligenceThe most impressive and well-reasoned use of AI
  • Excellence in Responsible AIThe best handling of fairness, privacy and possible misuse
  • Excellence in InnovationThe most original idea or approach
  • Excellence in Data & AnalyticsThe sharpest use of data, evidence and evaluation
  • Excellence in Social ImpactThe biggest potential benefit to people or communities
  • Excellence in CommunicationThe clearest, most convincing pitch or demo video
  • Excellence in STEM SpiritThe most inspiring “Fuel my ambition” video

* Winners must be eligible for admission onto their chosen UNF degree as part of the standard admission process, and must submit all documents the University of Niagara Falls Canada requires for that process. Prizes cannot be exchanged for money. Certificates of Excellence and an International STEM Day participation certificate, given to everyone who submits a complete project, are issued as digital certificates after results are announced.

    Official rules

    Rules of entry

    Rules marked S apply to everyone. Then follow the rules for your category: B for Bachelor's, M for Master's.

    Rules for all participants

    Applying to UNF

    You must apply to a University of Niagara Falls Canada program at your category's level for a 2027 intake, by the time winners are announced.

    Registration

    Every team member registers individually on this page by 28 February 2027 at 23:59 Toronto time, using the same team name.

    “Fuel my ambition” video

    Every participant uploads a 1 to 2 minute video when registering, telling us who they want to become and how STEM, their chosen specialisation, Canada and UNF will power them there. You must appear on camera and speak in your own words.

    Teams

    Enter alone or in a team of up to three. All members of a team must be in the same category. You can be in one team only.

    Deadline

    Your registration, “Fuel my ambition” video and project must all be submitted between 26 October 2026 and 28 February 2027 at 23:59 Toronto time. Your project must be created for this hackathon.

    Using AI tools

    AI assistants and pre-trained models are allowed. Name every tool you used and what for. Judges score what you added; undisclosed AI-generated work is disqualified.

    Data and privacy

    Use only public, synthetic or self-collected data you have the right to use. Do not use personal data about real people without their consent. Cite every data source.

    Conduct

    Be respectful to other participants, mentors and judges. Harassment, cheating or sharing another team's work leads to disqualification.

    Judging and results

    A panel from the University of Niagara Falls Canada judges each category separately. Winners are announced on 17 March 2027. The panel's decision is final.

    Prize conditions

    To receive a prize you must be eligible for admission onto your chosen UNF degree through its standard admission process, and submit every document it requires. Merit-based scholarships are conditional on admission and enrolment and are not transferable. No prize can be exchanged for money.

    Ticket to campus

    One one-way economy ticket from your home country to Niagara Falls for the start of your first term. Visas, insurance and other travel costs are your responsibility.

    Use of your entry and video

    You keep ownership of your work. By registering, you allow the University of Niagara Falls Canada to use your personal video, your project video, your name, image and project title to promote the hackathon, International STEM Day and UNF.

    Privacy

    Your documents are used only to run the hackathon and process your university application, and are shared only with the University of Niagara Falls Canada.

    Category B · Bachelor's rules

    Eligibility

    You have completed, or will complete, secondary school (Grade 12, A-levels, IB or equivalent) by August 2027 and are 16 or older on 28 February 2027.

    Program

    You are applying to a UNF honours bachelor's degree: Business Administration, Biomedical Sciences or Bioveterinary Science.

    What to build

    An AI solution concept with a working prototype. A no-code tool, chatbot builder, spreadsheet model, clickable mock-up or simple code all count.

    Pitch video

    2 to 3 minutes, MP4 or MOV, up to 300 MB. At least one team member appears on camera. Show the problem, your idea and the prototype in action.

    Pitch deck

    PDF, up to 8 slides: problem, who it helps, how the AI works, prototype screenshots, and what you would build next.

    Prototype link

    Optional. A link judges can open, or screenshots in the deck.

    Category M · Master's rules

    Eligibility

    You hold, or will complete by the start of your intake, a bachelor's degree or equivalent, and have not yet started a master's degree.

    Program

    You are applying to a UNF master's degree, such as the Master of Computer Science in Applied Artificial Intelligence, Master of Data Analytics or Master of Management.

    Working code

    Your solution must run. Share it in a GitHub or GitLab repository judges can open, with a README and run instructions. The project must be created for this hackathon.

    Evaluation

    Measure how well your solution works with suitable metrics (for example accuracy, F1, error rates or a user test) and compare it with a simple baseline.

    Technical report

    PDF, up to 8 pages: problem, data, method, results, limitations, and a responsible-AI section on bias, privacy and possible misuse.

    Demo video

    3 to 5 minutes, MP4 or MOV, up to 500 MB. At least one team member appears on camera and walks through a live demo.

    Questions

    FAQ

    What is International STEM Day?

    International STEM Day, on 8 November, celebrates science, technology, engineering and mathematics and encourages young people to explore them. The UNF AI Hackathon is held to celebrate it.

    Which category should I choose?

    Choose the level of the UNF program you are applying to. If you are applying to an honours bachelor's degree, enter Bachelor's. If you are applying to a master's degree, enter Master's.

    Do I need to know how to code?

    Not in the Bachelor's category: a no-code prototype or a clickable mock-up is fine. In the Master's category you must submit working code.

    Where does the hackathon take place?

    Online. You work from wherever you are and upload your project on this page by 28 February 2027.

    Can I enter alone?

    Yes. Solo entries and teams of up to three are judged together within each category.

    Can a Bachelor's and a Master's applicant be in the same team?

    No. Every member of a team must be in the same category, because the two categories are judged against different rules.

    Do I need to have applied to UNF already?

    No. You can register now and complete your UNF application in parallel. You must have applied by 17 March 2027 to receive a prize.

    Can I submit early?

    Yes, and we recommend it. You can register and submit your project any time from 26 October 2026 until 28 February 2027 at 23:59 Toronto time. The deadline does not move.
